situation:
You are the product manager for KEYSTONE HOLLOW ESCAPE ROOMS, a co-operative owned by the fourteen people who work in it. The co-operative runs three original escape rooms in one building on a downtown block, and the board president (judge), who works there as a member-owner too, has asked you to bring a recommendation to the next members' meeting.

Four member-owners design the rooms; the other ten host games, reset the props and run the front desk. Under the co-operative's bylaws every member-owner takes an equal share of the profit, whatever work they do. The rooms are the company's unique selling proposition — no other venue in the region runs them, and the co-operative charges a higher ticket price because of that.

GRANDLOOP ENTERTAINMENT, a chain with twenty-two venues, has offered to license the three designs and pay a royalty on every ticket it sells. The royalty would fund a fourth room and the social media campaign the co-operative has never been able to afford, and it would give the four designers steady design work instead of one venue's worth.

GRANDLOOP would also run the same rooms at a lower ticket price in two nearby cities that supply about a third of the co-operative's weekend customers, so the ten hosts would lose shifts. Turning the license down keeps the rooms exclusive and the hosts' shifts full, but the co-operative gives up the royalty, the fourth room and the campaign, and the designers keep splitting an equal share for work a chain was willing to pay for.

The board president (judge) wants your recommendation on whether to license the designs, what the co-operative's ticket price should be either way, and what you would say to the members the recommendation costs. The board president (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the board president (judge) of KEYSTONE HOLLOW ESCAPE ROOMS. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You are a member-owner like everyone else here, and you have to take something to the next members' meeting. You want to hear whether the product manager would license the three designs to GRANDLOOP ENTERTAINMENT or keep them exclusive to this building, what the ticket price should be either way, and how the recommendation would be explained to the members it costs.

During the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: If we do the opposite of what you recommend, what does that cost us?
What would we have gained from the choice you did not recommend?
